metadata.title: About | Alessio Quagliara
metadata.description: Who I am: web developer, Computer Engineering student (Intelligent Systems). I worked at Spotex, and today I also work in a warehouse.

hero.title: I build web applications. And I study.
hero.intro: I'm Alessio. I study Computer Engineering, Intelligent Systems track. At Spotex I built websites and web applications; today I also work in a warehouse. I use AI when I write code, but it's not the story: here you'll find the projects and what I'm learning.

principles.title: Four rules. I learned them the hard way.

items.title: Architectural pragmatism
items.text: The simplest solution that holds. No microservices for a contact form: I've done my time with overengineering.

items.title: Build in Public
items.text: Projects, numbers and mistakes go on the blog. Even the ones that make me look bad.

items.title: Hardware, out of curiosity
items.text: I'm studying Arduino, ESP32 and C to understand what sits under the software. Lab stuff, not client work.

items.title: Long-term maintainability
items.text: Code you can still read in two years, even if someone else opens it. Fewer parts, fewer surprises.

steps.title: My first e-commerce, never launched
steps.text: Car parts, a 14-day Shopify trial and no launch. First lesson: an idea isn't enough.

steps.title: Lyara and dropshipping
steps.text: Shopify, ads, copy, content. I lost money and gained a trade.

steps.title: Be Social
steps.text: My first web agency. Clients yes, margins no. That's when I moved everything to development.

steps.title: Spotex SRL
steps.text: A software house founded with partners, then closed. I built websites and web applications for clients there. I learned more there than in any course.

steps.title: LinkBay-CMS
steps.text: Born as a platform for agencies, trademark filed in 2025. Now I'm cutting it down to what matters: an SEO tool for decaying content.

steps.title: RStudy and PivotCut
steps.text: An app to study without the chaos and a macOS app for 2D animation, heading to its first release on itch.io. Built in public.

steps.title: Automation technician
steps.text: PLCs, electronics, networks. That's where I learned software sooner or later touches something physical.

steps.title: Arduino and ESP32
steps.text: Prototypes on a cutting mat, for learning: sensors, lean firmware, data sent to a backend.

steps.title: n8n and Node-RED
steps.text: Flows that connect tools and APIs. Useful to see how systems talk to each other.

steps.title: Back to C
steps.text: To understand what happens underneath: memory, I/O, performance. I write about it on the blog.

steps.title: Local AI
steps.text: I'm trying local models with Ollama and llama.cpp. I wrote about it on the blog.

steps.title: Automation Technician diploma
steps.text: Istituto Tecnico Padri Somaschi. The basics: automation, electronics, PLCs.

steps.title: Full Stack Web Developer
steps.text: MUSA Formazione. Frontend, backend and databases, end to end.

steps.title: Business diploma (AFM)
steps.text: ITES Caio Plinio Secondo. Accounting and marketing: useful when a product also has to make economic sense.

steps.title: Computer Engineering
steps.text: UNINETTUNO, Intelligent Systems. AI, embedded, IoT, databases.

stack.title: What I use, and what for
stack.hint: Hover or tap a badge to see where I use it.

items.name: Python
items.use: Scripts, APIs and integrations. My everyday language.

items.name: Flask
items.use: Lean backends: webhooks, APIs, internal dashboards.

items.name: Quart
items.use: Async Flask, when lots of calls are waiting around.

items.name: Full stack web
items.use: From database to interface, deploy included.

items.name: Jinja2
items.use: Server-rendered pages with Flask: simple, fast, easy to maintain.

items.name: Multi-tenant
items.use: Many clients on one platform, data never mixed. See LinkBay-CMS.

items.name: HTMX
items.use: Interactivity without a JavaScript framework: HTML asks, the server answers.

items.name: C
items.use: Algorithms, memory, firmware. C is the fun part.

items.name: ESP32
items.use: I'm studying it: sensors and built-in Wi-Fi.

items.name: PLC
items.use: Where my diploma started: logic and industrial automation.

items.name: n8n
items.use: Automations between tools and APIs, as experiments.

items.name: Node-RED
items.use: Event-driven flows, handy when devices are involved.

items.name: Docker
items.use: In production: same environment everywhere, deploys without surprises.

items.name: Ollama & llama.cpp
items.use: Local models, to experiment without sending data out.

metadata.title: Education | Alessio Quagliara
metadata.description: Continuous education path across automation, software development, business perspective, and a Computer Engineering degree focused on intelligent systems.

education.title: Education built across engineering, software, and real systems
education.intro: It comes from the intersection of engineering, software development, and business perspective. Today the focus is AI, intelligent systems, and real solution design.
education.learningStatement: Continuous learning is not filler work: it's how I connect technical growth and long-term vision.

items.title: Bachelor's Degree in Computer Engineering - Intelligent Systems
items.description: University path focused on advanced programming, artificial intelligence, machine learning, neural networks, embedded systems, IoT, cybersecurity, and databases, with attention to intelligent systems and software design.

items.title: Diploma in Administration, Finance and Marketing
items.description: A path that strengthened my understanding of accounting, marketing, business logic, and project sustainability, adding a perspective that is useful when building software products and services.

items.title: Full Stack Web Developer Certification
items.description: An intensive path focused on end-to-end web application design and development, which consolidated practical foundations across frontend, backend, databases, and product logic.

items.title: Diploma in Automation Technology
items.description: Technical training that built the foundations of my relationship with industrial automation, electronics, networks, and programming, and still shapes how I think about systems, hardware, and real-world integration.
